methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Growth → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.2x) to $47M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Transportation (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 3 same-sector peers exist in Transportation, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Pivotal operates in the Transportation sector at the Growth stage, backed by Page. The relevant comp universe includes three private peers—Rivian, The Boring Company, and Einride—though none meet narrow same-stage or adjacent-stage filtering criteria, limiting peer-median applicability. No public Transportation comparables at similar scale were identified.

Given data constraints, the Stage-Progression method is the primary applicable lens. Using $47M in total raised as a valuation proxy and applying a 1.2x step-up multiplier typical for Growth-stage advancement yields an implied valuation of $56M. This approach assumes Pivotal's capital deployment and progress track typical Growth-stage scaling dynamics. The peer-median method was not applied due to insufficient same-stage and adjacent-stage datapoints within the Transportation peer set; a broader sector median would risk conflating disparate business models and maturity profiles.

The triangulated valuation range is $48M to $64M, with a median of $56M. This range reflects the stage-progression anchor and a reasonable variance band around it, though the single-method foundation warrants acknowledgment of elevated uncertainty. Key sensitivities include the relevance of the 1.2x multiplier to Pivotal's specific operational progress and the company's capital efficiency relative to peer deployment patterns. Additional comp density at equivalent stage and tier would strengthen conviction in this range.
